summary: The root W-K-Z generally means to strike or beat. It can specifically refer to striking with a fist, especially on the chin, or pushing someone. It also encompasses piercing with a spear or goading.
lane: 1 وَكَزَهُ ذ , (S, Msb,) aor. يَكِزُهُ , (Msb,) inf. n. وَكْزٌ , (Msb, K,) He struck, or beat him, (S, Msb,) [with anything,] as, for ex., with a staff, or stick: (TA:) or it signifies, (Msb,) or signifies also (S) he struck, or beat, him with his fist upon his chin: (S, Msb:) or, accord. to Ks, i. q. لَكَمَهُ ; (Msb;) [i. e.] he struck, or beat, him with his fist. (A, K.) -b2- He pushed, or impelled, or repelled, him. (S, Msb, K.) -b3- He pierced him (Ks, K, * TK) with a spear. (TK.) -b4- He goaded him. (TA.) -b5- He broke his nose. (T, TA.)
